title: Dressed magnon dynamics in a Bose-Hubbard bath: retardation, pairing, entanglement and two-magnon scattering
authors: Andrés N. Cáliz, Arnau Riera, Enrique Rico, João Barata, Marcin Płodzień
abstract: We study one- and two-magnon dynamics in a spin-$1/2$ XX chain coupled to a tunable Bose-Hubbard bath. The XX Hamiltonian transports the magnons, while the bath dresses their motion and mediates an effective attraction. A single magnon forms a mobile polaron whose retarded bosonic cloud reduces its velocity below the static Lang-Firsov prediction and generates magnon-boson entanglement. In the weak-dressing, off-resonant mobile regime, the residual velocity deficit and entanglement are governed by the excitation weight of the cloud, as captured by perturbation theory and tensor network-based real-time simulations. Transport therefore provides a model-calibrated proxy for entanglement without joint-state reconstruction. When two clouds overlap, the bath mediates a finite-range attraction, yielding finite-size evidence for a compact two-magnon bound state and a transient post-scattering signature. On-site bath interactions suppress local boson number fluctuations and stiffen the bath response, reducing entanglement and weakening ground-state binding. Bath deformability thus emerges as a common control parameter for magnon transport, entanglement, and bath-mediated pairing.
summary: This paper models magnon dynamics in a quantum magnet coupled to a bosonic bath, revealing that the bath dressing causes the magnon to form a polaron. The key finding is that the measurable slowdown of the magnon's velocity quantifies the entanglement between the magnon and the bath, while the bath also mediates an attractive interaction leading to magnon pairing.
main_problem: The study investigates one- and two-magnon dynamics in a spin-1/2 XX chain coupled to a tunable Bose-Hubbard bath, focusing on the interplay between retardation, pairing, and entanglement.
main_result: The bath mediates an effective attraction between two magnons, leading to a bound state, while the measurable velocity deficit of a single magnon serves as a proxy for quantifying magnon-boson entanglement.
method: The authors employ a combination of polaron transformations, tensor network simulations (MPS), and Green's function techniques to analyze the coupled dynamics.
model_or_system: The system consists of a spin-1/2 XX chain coupled to a Bose-Hubbard bath via a density-coupling interaction. The dynamics are analyzed by treating the magnon as a polaron dressed by the bosonic bath.
key_observables: Velocity deficit ($\delta v$), magnon-boson entanglement entropy ($S_{mb}$), and the effective two-magnon binding potential ($V(r)$).
important_parameters: Bath deformability (controlled by on-site repulsion $U$), coupling strength ($\lambda$), and the ratio of bath frequency to hopping ($t_B/\omega_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as the single-field coherent-state ansatz and the weak-coupling limit for relating $\delta v$ to entanglement.
figures_summary: Figures compare coherent-state vs. many-body dynamics, show the time evolution of entanglement entropy during polaron formation, and plot the relationship between late-time entanglement and the velocity deficit.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the single-magnon polaron dynamics to establish the velocity deficit as an entanglement proxy, then examining the two-magnon sector to derive the bath-mediated attraction, and finally identifying bath deformability as the universal control parameter.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable link (velocity deficit) between transport properties and non-local quantum correlations (entanglement) in a system relevant to quantum magnetism and strongly correlated materials.
